scope: Read-only example compatibility review of Phase 10 library changes. No example execution, benchmark, figure verification or source edits were performed for this record.
all_example_ast_verification: Owned by the final Phase 10 verification evidence; this read-only review does not claim a separate syntax or execution run.

library_implications.effect: Configured public homogeneous calls retain source-reference context, locking, identity, status and optional availability. Existing property[row, column] indexing in spinodal_lines.py remains applicable.

Saturation branches contain one critical state plus N subcritical states, giving N+1 rows. Pseudocritical curves contain at most N_points ordinary states after source-domain filtering, without a prepended critical state. Quality-grid axes are (quality, temperature). Critical optional fields can be unavailable.
library_implications.pseudo_pure_limit: HEOS Air/R410A QT grids accept endpoint qualities 0 and 1; interior qualities raise an explicit unsupported-operation error with PQ guidance. REFPROP's supported fractional QT route remains distinct.

library_implications.effect: Pure-fluid two-phase interior cp and heat-capacity ratio are unavailable, while cv follows the repaired equilibrium derivative. Copied endpoint-averaging formulas in the examples require a scientific review rather than restoration merely to match historical output.

Outputs contain canonical thermodynamic property names, with no algorithmic x or smoothing-factor sigma fields. sigma retains its surface-tension alias. Blended states have a distinct model/reference identity, their interior phase flag is unavailable, and exact endpoints preserve selected-branch optional values.

Direct homogeneous density/temperature aliases need no guess. Other inverse calls require valid positive density/temperature guesses and valid settings. Finite targets, unsupported properties and independent final residual checks can expose previously unnoticed failed or stationary solves.

remaining_findings.reason: Default high-level sweeps need actual full-resolution execution and figure/numerical checks after the library repair. Inactive low-level branches read aliases from canonical raw mappings and operate on a raw source handle; revise those branches deliberately without changing scientific defaults. No minimal active-source edit was required by this read-only review.

The removed library grid-conversion helper is repaired and shape/indexing is documented. Dense EOS grids, branch/domain behavior, optional-property plotting and complete figures still require deliberate execution; no old timeout or failure was promoted to a pass.

Check continuation guesses and root failure handling throughout the actual scientific sweeps, keeping equilibrium, homogeneous and blended state collections separate by model identity. Validate diagnostics under their declared physical definitions.

Review copied two-phase formulas and actual differentiation constraints against the repaired model. The saturation script retains an obsolete nested state schema and removed collection helper. Replace those scientific/data-flow assumptions with supported endpoint/state APIs and independent checks while preserving locally undefined properties. Dormant copied kernels are not validated by successful execution of another active body.

Calls already use valid high-level aliases and explicit guesses; direct homogeneous density/temperature calls remain supported without a guess. Their historical success remains a checkpoint outcome until actual programs are rerun against the final source.

limitations: Library unit/integration tests are recorded separately and do not establish full example, plot or application acceptance.
The original 65-file execution audit and its outcome counts remain historical; this review does not claim a rerun of those programs.
No example equations, resolutions, model bounds, solver tolerances, iteration budgets or defaults were relaxed or edited.
